references.text: Sarah was childless and had no children – a direct parallel to Rebekah's infertility.
God remembered Rachel and heard her prayer. He opened her womb, and she became pregnant.
Hannah was childless and prayed earnestly to the Lord for a child. The Lord heard her prayer, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Samuel.
He lets the barren woman live in the house as a joyful mother with children. Hallelujah!
The angel told Zechariah that his prayer had been heard, and his wife Elizabeth would bear him a son – a parallel to answered prayers for infertility.
A parallel between Abraham's and Isaac's prayers to open wombs, emphasizing God's sovereignty over fertility.
Paul uses the event as theological proof of God's sovereign election independent of natural conditions.
A thematic parallel showing God's pattern of opening wombs for barren women in the history of the patriarchs.
Strong thematic parallel: God's intervention to give children to barren women (Rebekah and Ruth).
